title: CLIP: learn to match images and text
subtitle: Follow three image-caption pairs through two encoders, a matching matrix, a contrastive loss, and a real update. Then keep the encoders fixed and change the candidate descriptions.
audience: Deep-learning students who have studied image encoders and contrastive learning
centralLabel: One score for an image and a candidate description

sections.title: Pixels and words become comparable vectors
Compare every image with every caption
A wrong match changes both encoders
The candidate text supplies the classifier
A match score is not a truth judgment

legendTitle: Whole-image and whole-text vectors, not attention values
provenance: The offline example uses three 4×4 images, a trainable 16×3 pixel map, and an 11×3 bag-of-words text map. Every table is computed from the disclosed parameters, including exact normalization gradients. This is a CLIP-style teaching toy, not pretrained CLIP; its trained checkpoint is fitted only to these three pairs.
footer: Learn matching representations; keep the encoders fixed when supplying candidate text.
